scenes.title: Picture the box being pulled

beats.text: Consider a box pulled along a smooth, level floor by a rope sloping upwards. Watch the box speed up to the right.
It stays on the floor. The pull acts partly forwards and partly upwards, so it affects both the motion and the floor’s support.
We will find the box’s mass and the force from the floor. First, here is the whole question.

scenes.title: The whole question

beats.text: A force of twenty newtons pulls the box at sixty degrees above the horizontal.
It accelerates to the right at two metres per second squared.
Take g as ten metres per second squared.
The floor is smooth and horizontal. Contact is maintained. Only the pull, weight and normal reaction act.
Find the mass, m, and the upward normal reaction, R. Which part of the pull moves the box forwards?

scenes.title: Resolve the pull into two components

beats.text: Draw a right angled triangle. The original force is the hypotenuse. The given angle is measured from the horizontal.
Cosine is adjacent over hypotenuse, so the horizontal component H equals F cosine theta.
Substitute twenty and sixty degrees: twenty cosine sixty gives ten newtons to the right.
Sine is opposite over hypotenuse, so the vertical component V equals F sine theta.
Twenty sine sixty gives ten root three newtons upwards. Keep this exact value for now.
These components replace the angled force. They have the same combined effect. Do not add the original force again.

scenes.title: Use horizontal motion to find mass

beats.text: Take right as positive. Smooth means no friction. Weight and reaction are vertical, so only H contributes horizontally.
Newton’s second law: resultant force equals mass times acceleration.
In the horizontal direction, H equals m a.
Substitute the horizontal force, ten newtons, and acceleration, two metres per second squared.
Divide both sides by two. Mass equals ten divided by two.
The mass is five kilograms. That is the mass accelerated by this horizontal resultant.

scenes.title: Use vertical balance to find reaction

beats.text: The box stays on the horizontal floor, so its vertical acceleration is zero. Upwards, both reaction and the pull’s vertical component oppose weight.
Again, resultant force equals mass times acceleration.
Vertically, R plus V minus m g equals zero.
Substitute ten root three for V, five for mass, and ten for g.
Rearrange: R equals fifty minus ten root three newtons.
So the normal reaction is thirty two point seven newtons, to three significant figures.
The upward pull reduces the floor’s support. Its vertical component matters, even though the vertical acceleration is zero.

scenes.title: On a slope, turn the resolving axes

beats.text: Now consider a box on a straight smooth ramp, inclined at theta to the horizontal. It stays in contact; any applied force P acts along the slope.
Choose directions parallel and perpendicular to the ramp. Reaction is already perpendicular. Weight still points vertically down.
Why is the angle beside weight also theta? Rotate the horizontal and the slope through a right angle: they become the vertical and the inward normal. Their angle stays the same.
In the weight triangle, the inward component is adjacent to theta, giving m g cosine theta.
The downhill component is opposite theta, giving m g sine theta.
There are no other perpendicular forces, and perpendicular acceleration is zero. So reaction minus the inward weight component equals zero.
Therefore R equals m g cosine theta. An extra perpendicular push or pull would change this equation.
Along the slope, resultant force equals m a. Taking uphill positive, P minus m g sine theta equals m a.

scenes.title: Check the angle, then combine components

beats.text: Suppose the angle is measured from the vertical instead. Is the horizontal component still force times cosine of that angle? Pause and check the triangle.
No. The horizontal side is now opposite the marked angle, so use sine. Adjacent uses cosine; opposite uses sine.
With several forces, add signed horizontal components, then signed vertical components. Their vector sum gives the resultant.
